Vaibhav ran out. On the charpai sat one steel bowl heaped with rewri and peanuts.
"That's for everyone," said Mama. "Bhupen, Vaibhav, the cousins, all of you."
Bhupen reached in first. Vaibhav watched his cousin's hand and grabbed with both of his, stuffing his kurta pockets.
"Vaibhav! Why so many?"

Monsoon week, Sunflower group. Written by Rekha, class teacher.
The rain kept us indoors all morning, so I put one tin of cream biscuits on the mat for snack time. I said it was for the whole group.
Raghav looked at the tin, then at the others, and took five biscuits at once. He held them against his chest. Two more children did the same. Within a minute the tin was empty and three children had none.
Raghav told me, "If I wait, they eat it all."
Next I counted biscuits into a paper cup for each child, and we talked about the empty tin. Raghav gave one back.

qa.a: Each child knew a fair share was saved for them, so there was no reason to rush and grab.

qa.a: They would likely feel sad and left out, since the others' quick grabbing emptied the tin before they had a turn.

grounding: Illustrates a young child grabbing from a shared tin of treats out of fear the group will finish it, so several children are left with nothing.

Urmila, you're fighting with your hostel about the washing machine? Let me tell you about our chawl tap. I'm Hansa, your old Masi, and at twenty-four I lived in a Mumbai chawl where forty families shared one tap and one tank.
Every morning there was shouting. People filled drums, washed scooters, left the tap open.

The water tanker came to the community garden only twice a week that summer, and the heat in Chennai had cracked the beds. Twelve families shared one tank.
Vidya, twenty-five, watched people drain it in a day. Some flooded their chillies; some came late and found nothing.
She had one evening before the next tanker. She drew a table on chart paper: each plot got two buckets, a morning slot, and a tick box. Elizabeth, from the next plot, agreed to check the tank level with her on alternate days. Anyone who took more would skip the next watering.
The first evening, Vidya carried exactly two buckets past everyone watching. By the second week, the tank lasted till the tanker came.

qa.a: Each plot had a fair limit, checking was shared with Elizabeth, the consequence was agreed, and Vidya followed the limit first where people could see.

qa.q: What is it like for a family who used to come late and find nothing?
qa.a: They can now count on their two buckets, so they feel treated fairly instead of left out.

grounding: Shows a young adult setting fair limits, shared checking and a consequence for a shared water tank in hot weather, and modelling the rule first.

Trisha and Chandrika were paired for the presentation on water purification. They were given two weeks. When I checked in on Day 6, each told me separately that the other was "handling the slides."
